transcript: Last night, I attended The Brothers Size at The Shed and it was outstanding. I wasn't familiar with this play by Tarell Alvin McCraney so I didn't know what to expect, but evidently it's a masterpiece — like, the kind of play I wanna go back and read. Centered around two brothers, recently reunited after one of them being in prison, this is an aching but beautiful play about systemic issues like the carceral system and the psychological toll it takes on people, as well as interpersonal themes like family and masculinity. The writing is pure poetry, and with strategically varying levels of ornamentation in the language, it's often the most simple and succinct lines that hit the hardest. I love the way this production is staged and directed, with stark and atmospheric lighting, circular and almost hypnotic blocking and percussive live music by Munir Zakee. And the performances from André Holland, Alani iLongwe and Malcolm Mays are all so delicate and rich with humor and sorrow. They had us crying and laughing and crying again, and they really left it all on the stage. I was especially impressed by Alani iLongwe’s physicality which added quite an entertaining and humorous layer to his performance without approaching caricature. And although there are a lot of funny moments, there's a profound heaviness to these characters with everything they've experienced and how they still experience the world around them. It's refreshing to see a play take on this kind of heaviness with such fearlessness and potency. I was genuinely so moved. I would highly recommend this production, especially if you haven't seen the play before. With that, another program for my collection.
